title: Egress floor (ipBlock CIDRs) over-blocks cluster-internal traffic on Cilium — breaks sessions/runs on enforcing CNIs
description: LIVE-FOUND on gtr (real Cilium) 2026-06-16 while running the session smoke test. BuildSmolAgentEgressPolicy (operator/internal/builders/serving_egress.go) builds the run/session egress floor as a k8s NetworkPolicy whose 'allow internal' rule is an ipBlock to private CIDRs (10.0.0.0/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, all ports). On kindnet this is a no-op (not enforced) so it 'works'; but Cilium resolves cluster destinations (pods/ClusterIP services) by ENDPOINT IDENTITY, not CIDR — service traffic is DNAT'd to the backend pod and evaluated against the pod identity, so the ipBlock CIDR rule does NOT match cluster-internal targets => DENIED. Result on gtr: the session worker's agentfs-init can't reach minio (AgentFS S3) and the agent can't reach NATS (turn delivery) — both cluster-internal — so the worker hangs at Init and sessions/runs that need any in-cluster dependency (minio/NATS/Qdrant) BREAK on any enforcing CNI. Fix: the floor must allow cluster-internal egress via identity-based rules — k8s NetworkPolicy podSelector/namespaceSelector to the needed services, or a Cilium-aware toEntities:[cluster] — not ipBlock CIDRs; and the operator should auto-allow the worker's known deps (the session NATS URL + the Agent's configured AgentFS S3 endpoint). Relates to rv1.2 (egress honesty) + c5r.20 (egress seam). Workaround for the gtr smoke test: an additive CiliumNetworkPolicy allowing the worker egress (classifier-blocked pending user OK).
notes: Fix implemented in PR #42 (branch fix/egress-floor-cilium-identity, commit 4b27403): buildEgressPolicy now prepends an identity-based namespaceSelector{} peer to the in-cluster rule alongside the RFC1918 CIDRs. namespaceSelector{} subsumes the worker's NATS + AgentFS-S3 deps (both in-cluster) without enumerating them. Unit test asserts the leading namespaceSelector. Live datapath PROVEN on gtr 2026-06-17: session worker (gtr-153) reaches minio (agentfs-init OK once bucket recreated) + NATS; z.ai glm-4.6 turn 5mSCVWHi4xpLwHiLUd6HXh completed end-to-end ('The capital of France is Paris.', 221 tokens). NOTE: that live run still had the manual CiliumNetworkPolicy chat-session-egress-allow in place — floor-ONLY verification (delete the manual CNP after deploying the PR image) is the remaining step, pending merge+release+redeploy to gtr.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #42 (merged af763a7). FLOOR-ONLY LIVE-VERIFIED on gtr (real Cilium) 2026-06-17: deployed operator:af763a7 (it updated the chat-session-egress NetworkPolicy in place to add a namespaceSelector{} peer), DELETED the manual CiliumNetworkPolicy chat-session-egress-allow, restarted the worker. Fresh worker's agentfs-init reached minio (exitCode 0, 0 restarts) and a z.ai glm-4.6 turn completed end-to-end (turnId 5mSCVWHi4xpLwHiLUd6Hfm -> 'Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.', 214 tokens) with ZERO CiliumNetworkPolicy present. The identity-based namespaceSelector floor permits cluster-internal egress (minio/NATS) on Cilium; the public 80/443 rule covers z.ai. Manual workaround no longer needed.

title: kind=fanout — Send-style runtime map-reduce tool
description:
As a platform engineer authoring a loop-mode Agent, I want to declare a kind=fanout tool so that a single LLM tool call can fan out N parallel child AgentRuns over a runtime-computed list of items, fold their outputs via a chosen reducer, and return one observation — enabling Send-style map-reduce without blocking the loop on sequential A2A calls.

The feature adds ToolKind="fanout" to the existing ToolSpec discriminated union (pkg/agentmodel/v1/types.go), backed by a new FanoutTargetSpec that names the target Agent, the reduce strategy (concat/merge/first-success), a per-item token ceiling, and a MaxParallel width cap. A new FanoutInvoker (pkg/agentruntime/invokers/invoker_fanout.go) factors the single-child spawn/poll/fold loop that currently lives inline in AgentRunInvoker into a shared helper (spawnAndPoll), then drives N of those helpers concurrently under a WidthLimiter sourced from pkg/turnmodel/team, folding child usages field-wise and applying the reducer to their outputs. Every child still passes the existing admitRunConcurrency gate in the AgentRun controller, MaxParallel is hard-clamped to a new FANOUT_MAX_WIDTH operator env injected by BuildAgentRunPod alongside the existing A2A env block, and recursion is bounded by inheriting the parent's A2A_DEPTH+1 / A2A_MAX_DEPTH guards unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- ToolKind='fanout' is present in Valid() and SupportedLoopToolKinds(); a loop-mode Agent webhook rejects a kind=fanout tool that references a cross-namespace Agent name containing a slash (D1 same-namespace enforcement identical to AgentTeam.ValidateAgentTeam's bare-name check).
- FanoutInvoker fans out exactly len(items) child AgentRuns concurrently, bounded to min(FanoutTargetSpec.MaxParallel, FANOUT_MAX_WIDTH from env); if FANOUT_MAX_WIDTH is absent the invoker returns an error immediately (fail-closed, D3 — no unbounded width blast).
- Every child AgentRun created by FanoutInvoker passes through admitRunConcurrency in the AgentRun controller (no bypass path); child creation uses Client.Create on the same in-cluster client as AgentRunInvoker, subject to the same per-namespace AgentRunQuota cap (D10).
- Each child is OwnerReferenced to the parent run using the literal AGENT_RUN_UID env value (not the pod's downward-API metadata.uid, which is the pod UID — the known bug documented in operator/internal/builders/agentrun.go line 64); children inherit the parent's A2A_DEPTH+1 label, and the invoker refuses to spawn if Depth >= MaxDepth (fail-closed recursion guard).
- Usage is folded field-wise from each completed child into the returned rt.Observation (Tokens summed, ToolCalls summed, CostUSDMilli summed); Usage.Add is never called (platform invariant: never Usage.Add, never gate on toolCalls).
- Partial failure semantics: concat and merge reducers return a partial result plus an error-count annotation when some children fail; first-success returns the first Completed child's output and cancel-deletes the remaining in-flight children (best-effort, same pattern as AgentRunInvoker's ctx-cancellation delete in Invoke). No child failure is silently dropped.
- The admission webhook for kind=fanout Tools rejects: MaxParallel < 0, an empty Ref.Name, an unknown Reduce enum value, and PerItemMaxTokens < 0 — mirroring ValidateAgentTeam's self-contained admission check (no cluster lookups).
- A table-driven unit test (using the existing fakeRunClient pattern from invoker_agent_test.go) covers: N=1 success, N=3 all-success concat fold, N=3 one-failure merge partial, first-success early-exit, depth-exceeded refusal, width-clamp refusal when FANOUT_MAX_WIDTH absent, and field-wise usage accumulation across children.

TEST PLAN:
- pkg/agentruntime/invokers/invoker_fanout_test.go — table-driven unit tests with fakeRunClient (same pattern as invoker_agent_test.go): covers all-success concat/merge, partial-failure with errors surfaced, first-success early-exit with in-flight cancel, depth-exceeded refusal, width-clamped fail-closed (FANOUT_MAX_WIDTH=0), and field-wise usage accumulation across N children; run with go test -race ./pkg/agentruntime/invokers/...
- pkg/agentmodel/v1/ — table tests for ValidateFanoutTool (every rejection case: empty ref name, slash in ref name, unknown reducer, MaxParallel<0, PerItemMaxTokens<0) and for the ToolKind.Valid() and SupportedLoopToolKinds() extensions; run with go test -race ./pkg/agentmodel/v1/...
- Refactor regression: existing invoker_agent_test.go must pass unchanged after the spawnAndPoll factoring — the only behavioral contract is AgentRunInvoker.Invoke, which the tests exercise end-to-end via fakeRunClient; run with go test -race ./pkg/agentruntime/invokers/... before and after subtask 3 to confirm no regression.
- Webhook validation: add a test in operator/internal/webhooks/ (following agentteam_webhook_test.go pattern if it exists, else a plain unit test calling the webhook's validate method directly) that exercises ValidateFanoutTool through the webhook shim for both valid and invalid fanout Tool objects.
- Width-limiter concurrency: a test using a fakeRunClient with a configurable delay on Get (simulating a slow child) that verifies: with FanoutMaxWidth=2 and 4 items, at most 2 children are in-flight simultaneously (checking WidthLimiter.InUse() peaks at 2, using pkg/turnmodel/team.WidthLimiter.InUse() which already exists for observability); run with -race to catch concurrent-map or double-release bugs.
- make build passes after all changes (both root module and operator module compile); make test passes with -race; no new test is disabled or skipped.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Should WireFanoutInvoker build its own in-cluster client.Client or accept the one already built by WireAgentInvoker? Sharing avoids two in-cluster configs and two cache instances, but requires a refactor of WireAgentInvoker's signature so it returns the client (currently it is self-contained). The alternative is a small package-level var, which introduces mutable global state — likely wrong. Decide before subtask 5.
- What is the exact JSON shape of args that the LLM passes to a fanout tool? The proposal says { items: [] }, but the LLM sees this as part of the tool's inputSchema. Should items be an array of any (opaque per-item JSON), a typed array constrained by a sub-schema, or a fixed string list? This determines what ValidateFanoutTool checks for PerItemMaxTokens (it bounds per-child, but the input schema must describe what a single item is). The operator passes inputSchema verbatim — the author defines it in the Tool CR.
- Reduce='first-success' cancel-deletes remaining in-flight children via best-effort Client.Delete. The existing AgentRunInvoker does the same on ctx cancellation (invoker_agent.go lines 155-159). However, fanout children are N concurrent goroutines sharing a context — when one succeeds, the invoker cancels the shared context, and each goroutine's select-on-ctx.Done branch fires. Should each goroutine's cleanup delete its own child (N deletes), or should the caller collect the in-flight names and delete in a single loop? The N-goroutine-each-delete approach is simpler but produces N parallel delete calls.
- The merge reducer must deep-merge N JSON objects. Deep-merge semantics (key-last-wins vs error-on-conflict) need a decision before implementation; the proposal says 'key-last-wins' but this is lossy for duplicate keys. Should merge instead be defined as 'union of keys, error on conflicting values for the same key'? This affects what the LLM author can rely on.
- FANOUT_MAX_WIDTH operator default is proposed as 64. Is that the right ceiling for the D10 blast-radius concern? The admission queue in admitRunConcurrency is the real central cap, but a fanout of 64 children against a namespace cap of 10 means 54 children queue immediately. Should FANOUT_MAX_WIDTH also check the remaining namespace concurrency headroom at invoke time (a read of namespaceRunState) or rely entirely on the admission queue to serialize them? The latter is simpler and consistent with how A2A works today.
- The A2A RBAC Role (AgentA2ARole in operator/internal/builders/agent_a2a_rbac.go) already grants create/get/list/watch on agentruns. Fanout children are also AgentRuns, so the existing Role covers them — but should the Agent controller wire the A2A Role for an Agent that declares a kind=fanout tool even if it declares no kind=agent tool? Currently (agent_controller.go, not read) the Role is presumably created only when the Agent has a kind=agent tool. Confirm this gating and extend it to include kind=fanout.

title: AgentWorkflow: declarative result-routed DAG CRD (StateGraph)
description:
As a platform engineer orchestrating multi-step agent pipelines, I want to declare a static, operator-evaluated DAG of AgentRuns with conditional routing between nodes based on prior-node output, so that I get reproducible, auditable control flow that cannot be hijacked by an agent choosing its own next step.

AgentWorkflow adds a new CRD whose controller walks a declared DAG level-by-level, materializing each ready node as a child AgentRun (same ownerRef-GC and admitRunConcurrency path as A2A children), polling terminal state, then evaluating outgoing conditional edges against the node's status.output via an operator-side allow-listed CEL expression (sandboxed, no I/O, predicate field reads explicitly banned on usage fields). The implementation mirrors the AgentTeam layering exactly: pure type in pkg/agentmodel/v1/agentworkflow.go with ValidateAgentWorkflow (acyclic check + endpoint existence + predicate compile-check), hand-written deepcopy in both zz_generated.deepcopy.go files, a hand-edited CRD YAML, a self-validation webhook (SetupAgentWorkflowWebhook following the agentteam_webhook.go shape), and a controller in operator/internal/controllers/agentmodel/ that uses RollUpTeamUsage for field-wise CumulativeUsage and AgentWorkflowOwnerRef (literal workflow UID, not downward-API metadata.uid) for subtree GC. A shared blackboard lives in a ~1 MiB ConfigMap keyed by workflow name; large payloads route through AgentFS or a secretRef side-channel.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- D1 same-namespace: every spec.nodes[].agentRef is a bare name; containsSlash() rejects cross-namespace refs at webhook admission AND in the reconciler fail-closed backstop (ValidateAgentWorkflow, mirroring ValidateAgentTeam).
- D3 fail-closed: the webhook rejects any predicate that does not compile against the allow-listed CEL environment at apply-time; the reconciler also re-validates at reconcile-time and sets status.phase=Failed/InvalidSpec on any predicate that now fails compilation (e.g., after operator upgrade narrows the environment).
- D10 admission-queue: child AgentRuns created by the workflow controller go through the normal Client.Create path and are therefore subject to admitRunConcurrency / AgentRunQuota per-namespace caps — no bypass.
- Cost observability-only: status.cumulativeUsage rolls up field-wise via RollUpTeamUsage; CostUSDMilli is never read in any routing predicate or gate condition; no code path gates DAG advancement on usage.toolCalls.
- Predicate safety: the CEL environment has NO access to usage fields (Steps, Tokens, ToolCalls, CostUSDMilli, WallClockUsed); attempting to reference them at compile-time produces a type-check error that fails the webhook.
- Acyclicity: ValidateAgentWorkflow runs a DFS cycle check over spec.edges at admission; a cycle causes immediate rejection with a descriptive error naming the cycle members.
- Subtree GC: each child AgentRun created by the controller carries an OwnerReference with the workflow's literal UID (types.UID(workflow.UID)), NOT a downward-API fieldRef, matching the AgentTeamOwnerRef pattern and avoiding the known A2A GC bug.
- START/END reserved nodes: exactly one node named START must exist; END is the terminal sink; the acyclicity check and topology walk treat them as sentinels and reject any spec that declares a node with a reserved name other than as the start/end.

TEST PLAN:
- pkg/agentmodel/v1/agentworkflow_test.go: table-driven unit tests (no external deps, pure Go) for ValidateAgentWorkflow — 12+ cases covering acyclicity DFS, START sentinel, endpoint existence, containsSlash D1 enforcement, and CEL predicate compile-check rejection of usage-field references. Run with go test -race ./pkg/agentmodel/v1/...
- pkg/agentmodel/v1/workflow_predicate_test.go: table tests for CompilePredicate and EvalPredicate — nil predicate=true, string-match predicate, false-branch predicate, malformed output JSON returns false (fail-closed), usage-field reference rejected at compile time. Run with go test -race ./pkg/agentmodel/v1/...
- operator/internal/controllers/agentmodel/agentworkflow_controller_test.go: fake-client controller tests (sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/client/fake, mirroring agentteam_controller_test.go) — linear DAG node materialization, conditional edge non-advancement, field-wise CumulativeUsage roll-up with stray-run exclusion, fail-closed on invalid spec, literal-UID owner-ref assertion. Run with go test -race ./operator/internal/controllers/agentmodel/...
- make envtest: run the controller-runtime envtest suite (operator/internal/controllers/envtest_suite_test.go) with the new AgentWorkflow CRD installed to confirm the controller registers, webhook fires, and at least one reconcile loop advances a simple linear workflow to Completed against a real apiserver. Verify no admitRunConcurrency bypass by seeding an AgentRunQuota with MaxConcurrentRuns=1 and asserting the second node's child run is held Pending until the first child's run slot frees.
- make test (root module -race): confirm the pure types and predicate evaluator compile and all existing tests remain green after adding cel-go to go.mod. Specifically re-run pkg/turnmodel/team/... tests to confirm RollUpTeamUsage is still correct (it is reused, not copied).

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Predicate DSL: the design calls for sandboxed CEL. cel-go is not currently in go.mod (confirmed). The addition is straightforward for the root module, but requires a conscious go get + go mod tidy. The alternative is a minimal JSONPath-compare DSL (zero new deps, 50 lines) that only supports output.field == "value" and output.field != "value". Which is the right scope for P0 — full CEL or minimal JSONPath-compare?
- Blackboard ConfigMap lifecycle: the spec says the shared blackboard lives in a ~1 MiB ConfigMap keyed by workflow name. Should the controller CREATE this ConfigMap at workflow-creation time (as an owned resource, GC'd on deletion), or should nodes write to it themselves (requires the node pod to have ConfigMap patch RBAC in the workflow's namespace)? The latter is richer but requires a new RBAC role and complicates the trust model.
- MaxDepth and A2A depth budget: workflow-spawned child AgentRuns are created by the controller (operator RBAC), not by an in-pod A2A invoker. They therefore start at A2A depth 0 (no DepthLabel). Should the workflow controller stamp a DepthLabel on each child based on its DAG level, or keep depth tracking separate from DAG level? If the child nodes themselves spawn further A2A children, the existing MaxDepth guard applies, but the workflow's own DAG depth is unrelated.
- Immutability of spec after workflow starts: should spec.nodes and spec.edges be immutable once the workflow enters Running phase (to prevent topology changes mid-execution), or should a DAG change restart the workflow? The webhook currently only validates self-consistency, not immutability. AgentTeam has no such restriction but a workflow mid-execution with a changed topology is undefined behavior.
- Parallel node materialization and width clamping: the controller as specified materializes all 'ready' nodes in a single reconcile pass. For wide DAGs this could burst the namespace's AgentRunQuota. Should the controller apply a workflow-level MaxConcurrentNodes cap (analogous to AgentTeam.spec.maxMembers / WidthLimiter in pkg/turnmodel/team/width.go) to spread materialization across reconcile cycles?
